dimension_justifications.soundness: The primary RR2 artifact is unusually strong and its temporary-copy replay passed, reconstructing 96 configurations, 96 timelines, 288 phase artifacts, eight attention-oracle values, and nine matched fault pairs from 536 raw artifacts. The lifecycle replay and historical GDN numerical replay also passed. However, the exact fully preregistered GDN evidence used by the paper is not replay-closed after anonymization, and the A4 transfer package omits its source and semantic replayer. These are substantive provenance gaps for two decision-relevant evidence objects.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is clear about denominators, captured-input boundaries, the negative A4 outcome, and the distinction between relational and independent oracles. It rebuilds successfully to 19 pages with anonymous PDF metadata. Presentation is weakened by a reproducibility statement placed after the references, stale cross-file provenance metadata, and a reviewer package whose blind status contradicts its contents.
dimension_justifications.contribution: An executable ownership and accounting audit for heterogeneous KV and recurrent state is useful, and the pointer-free phase witness plus mutation-tested replay is a concrete contribution. The evidence remains one positive model/runtime/schedule case; the different-runtime A4 experiment is correctly retained as a negative. This limits the general scientific contribution relative to broader KV-cache and serving anchors.

paper_summary: ForkAudit specifies seven phase-aware audit targets for hybrid attention-KV and recurrent GDN state, then validates them through a four-cell ownership factorial on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, selected attention and GDN numerical oracles, live fault injections, explicit allocator denominators, one same-adapter cancellation/reclamation lifecycle, and a negative Transformers DynamicCache transfer experiment.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest independently checked contribution is the manifest-bound RR2 offline replay: in a temporary copy it passed and reconstructed 96 four-cell factorial configurations, 96 ownership timelines, 288 phases, eight dense-attention oracle rows, nine matched fault pairs, and allocator results from 536 raw artifacts totaling 888785811 bytes. This verifies frozen-artifact consistency, not fresh GPU regeneration.
strengths: The top-level provenance audit passed twice without snapshot modification: 963 manifest members, 14 registered evidence IDs, 13 claim-linked IDs, 29 method rows, and 42 Python symbols resolved to the required snapshot SHA.

The manuscript and claim map consistently distinguish CPU/offline artifact replay from live GPU reproduction, PyTorch allocator counters from NVML or service capacity, and selected captured-input oracles from end-to-end correctness.
The temporary manuscript build completed successfully with BibTeX and produced a 19-page anonymous PDF with blank author metadata.
The lifecycle raw-first replay passed all eight shards and rejected stale-gate, zero-scrub, reservation-reassignment, and raw-manifest tampering.
The historical GDN replay package passed four clean rows and rejected four seeded faults, with only sub-micro NumPy/BLAS portability drift.

Dataset hashes, selected PG-19 objects/windows, model revision and weight-ledger hashes, seeds, environment versions, H20 hardware, fan-outs, schedules, tolerances, and claim boundaries are recorded at unusually high granularity.
A4 is reported honestly as a valid negative: all eight matched-clean ranks fail the frozen dense semantic threshold, so it is not used as positive runtime-portability evidence.
The included citation lock states both support and non-support boundaries for each citation and uses primary proceedings, DOI, arXiv, or official model sources for nearly all entries.
questions: Can the authors provide a manifest-first, one-command reviewer derivative for the fully preregistered GDN run itself, rather than directing reviewers to the earlier amended replay package?
Why are the seven A4 source files listed only by digest in source-manifest.json instead of being included, and where is the independent raw-to-aggregate A4 replay implementation?

Can the authors remove the organization-identifying container registry, platform job/trial and cluster identifiers, GPU UUIDs, and the embedded review-response-plan preimage from the blind package while retaining non-identifying cryptographic bindings?

Which package does integrated_results.json SHA c9773d54262aa0d2a3986cade79ec2f8bffdbfea0f27282944ccc7935eba992a identify, given that the shipped RR2 MANIFEST.json hashes to be5f55be72adcb1ab57747324a029d13906d39ec0d0e2efb05b883ac812cbff7?
Is a clean live-GPU reproduction intended to be part of the release, or is the artifact deliberately limited to replay of the frozen execution?

issues.location: PDF p.1 Abstract, p.7 Section 5.3, p.12 Reproducibility Statement, and p.17 Table 12; evidence/gdn_transition_oracle_preregistered_20260819d/ versus evidence/gdn_transition_oracle_replay/
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's claimed fully preregistered result is the fresh R6 package, but README.md's only GDN replay command targets gdn_transition_oracle_replay, whose PROVENANCE.json classifies it as verified_bounded_post_hoc_captured_input and says the amendment lacks immutable pre-execution binding. Directly invoking the shipped fully preregistered reference on its shipped redacted capture and preregistration fails with 'capture/preregistration binding drift': redaction changed preregistration bytes while the capture retained the original raw hash. Thus the exact A2/fresh-preregistration evidence object used in the paper is not reviewer-replayable as shipped.
issues.why_it_matters: The four GDN rows are the paper's only independent recurrent numerical check. Replaying numerically identical sidecars from an earlier amended run is not equivalent to verifying that the claimed fresh preregistration, capture, source, and result form one closed artifact.
issues.required_fix: Create a dedicated reviewer-safe package for the fully preregistered run containing the exact redacted preregistration, capture, reference source, internal derivative bindings, manifest, and one-command replay. Preserve original-to-derivative hash mappings separately and explicitly identify the historical amended package as contextual only.
issues.verification_test: In a clean extraction, run one documented command that first verifies the package file set and preregistration-to-capture binding, then recomputes all four clean and four faulty transitions from the fully preregistered sidecars. Require 4/4 clean passes, 4/4 fault rejections, the declared tolerances, and an explicit binding to the fresh preregistration ID.
issues.evidence_needed: A reclosed anonymous derivative and successful clean-environment replay log for E-R6-FULLY-PREREGISTERED-GDN-ORACLE.

issues.location: PDF p.12 Reproducibility Statement; top-level README.md; evidence/round_04_rr2_package/configuration/executed_configuration.anonymous.json and executed_source/gpu/launch_qcomem_qwen35_forkaudit_review_revision_8gpu.sh
issues.observed_evidence: The shipped RR2 command successfully replays frozen artifacts but does not regenerate the GPU execution. The original command is omitted; weights and PG-19 bytes are external; ENV_DIR is a private frozen environment; and the launcher requires numerous manually supplied paths and hashes, including the response-plan input. The manuscript also discloses that the live aggregate and later offline replay are not bound by one terminally closed run because pycache appeared after the frozen ledger.
issues.why_it_matters: Artifact replay gives strong evidence that archived receipts are internally consistent, but it cannot detect producer-side defects before capture and is not an independent reproduction of the core live execution. The distinction should remain explicit, and a reproducibility-grade release should make a fresh run feasible.
issues.required_fix: Provide a reviewer-safe live-rerun recipe with a public container or complete environment lock, one configuration file supplying all launcher variables, exact model/data acquisition and verification instructions, expected resource requirements, and expected terminal products. Prefer a fresh run that closes GPU execution, aggregation, cleanup, recursive source integrity, and replay under one run identifier.
issues.verification_test: On a clean compatible H20 environment, acquire external inputs by documented procedures, verify their frozen digests, execute one live command, and require all terminal closure stages plus an offline replay whose outputs and manifests bind to that same new run ID.
issues.evidence_needed: A new independently executable live run and single-run terminal-closure receipts.

ethics_concerns: No substantive research-ethics concern was identified. The exposed organization and platform identifiers are a double-blind submission-integrity problem rather than an ethics allegation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by a fresh isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. The subagent was read-only, received only the frozen round-07 submission snapshot and specified review protocol/rubric/calibration files, and did not communicate with other reviewers.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A reclosed, one-command replay of the exact fully preregistered GDN run.
Complete A4 executed source plus a deterministic raw-to-aggregate semantic replay.
A clean anonymous snapshot with no response-plan or infrastructure-identity leakage.
A fresh live GPU reproduction with one run ID binding execution, aggregation, cleanup, terminal source closure, and offline replay.
Positive transfer to a clean second runtime or hybrid model under an independent semantic oracle, if the paper seeks a broader claim.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to reproduce the current RR2 replay outputs or any mismatch in its 536 raw-artifact ledger.
Evidence that the fully preregistered GDN sidecars differ scientifically from the historical amended replay beyond disclosed numerical portability drift.
Inability to produce A4 source bytes matching the frozen source-manifest hashes.
Any attempt to reinterpret the A4 negative as positive runtime-portability evidence.
Evidence that exposed platform identifiers or the response-plan artifact identify the authors or influenced blind reviewer isolation.
review_limitations: Per the isolation instruction, no external web access or repository path outside the specified snapshot and reviewer protocol files was used; citation existence and local support were assessed from the included bibliography and citation lock rather than independently opening every cited source.
The live GPU experiments were not rerun because the required H20 environment, model weights, and PG-19 bytes are external. Findings distinguish fresh reproduction from snapshot artifact replay.
The embedded review-experiment-response-plan.json was not opened or interpreted.
